🚨 BIG NEWS: $NBIS NEBIUS IMPROVES AI TRAINING THROUGHPUT ON 192 NVIDIA B300 GPUs WITHOUT ADDING A SINGLE GPU.

This is a pretty bug technical update from Nebius.

Nebius tested NUMA-aware process affinity on a DeepSeek V3 pretraining workload running across 192 NVIDIA B300 GPUs using Megatron Bridge on its managed Kubernetes platform.

The results? Mean training step time decreased by 1.11%, while model throughput per GPU increased by 1.13%.

Now, 1.13% might not sound impressive initially. But when you're operating thousands of expensive GPUs, even a small improvement in utilization can have meaningful economic value.

Modern GPU servers have multiple CPU sockets and NUMA domains. Each CPU has faster access to its local memory and PCIe connected devices. When training processes get scheduled across the wrong NUMA domains, they can introduce unnecessary memory traffic, latency and communication overhead.

Nebius tested exclusive NUMA binding, which keeps processes closer to their local CPU, memory and GPU resources.

The important part is that they're improving performance through infrastructure level optimization rather than buying additional compute.

Imagine a hypothetical 100,000 GPU deployment achieving the same 1.13% throughput improvement. That's roughly the training throughput equivalent of adding 1,130 GPUs, assuming the improvement scales consistently.

Of course, this benchmark doesn't prove the same gains will hold across every model, cluster or workload.

Nebius is operating in a market where GPUs are extremely expensive, power availability is constrained and customers care about how quickly they can train models.

If Nebius can consistently extract more useful compute from the same hardware, customers can finish training workloads faster while Nebius potentially improves the competitiveness and economics of its cloud platform.

This wasn't a synthetic GPU benchmark. Nebius used a DeepSeek V3 pretraining workload with Megatron Bridge, which makes the result more relevant to actual large model training.

This is what separates simply renting NVIDIA GPUs from building a serious AI cloud platform.

Anybody with enough capital can purchase GPUs. Getting those GPUs to operate efficiently across CPU topology, memory, networking, containers and distributed training software is an entirely different engineering problem.

Nebius is showing that it's paying attention to that layer and as its GPU infrastructure scales, these seemingly small optimizations could become increasingly important to its customers and its own infrastructure economics.

이번 반박은 단순한 부인이 아니라 구체적인 기술 설명과 수치를 담고 있습니다.

1. WSE 수명 논란

Culper는 웨이퍼 수명을 약 1.5~2.5년으로 추정했습니다.

Cerebras는 TSMC의 105°C·10년 연속 작동 인증과 실제 CS-3 운영 온도를 근거로 수명 단축 주장을 반박했습니다.

다만 이론적인 열화 수명이 실제 장비의 보증 수명을 의미하지는 않습니다.

2. Paricon 소재와 열팽창

CEO는 Culper가 지목한 PariPoser 소재를 사용하지 않으며, 해당 소재를 사용한 제품을 출하한 적도 없다고 밝혔습니다.

열팽창 문제는 유연한 연결 구조와 온도 제어 기술로 대응한다고 설명했습니다.

3. 더미 연산과 전력 소비

더미 연산은 급격한 전력·온도 변화를 방지하기 위한 의도적인 제어 기술이라고 반박했습니다.

4. 웨이퍼 폐기율

2024년 CS-3 도입 이후 배치된 웨이퍼 중 폐기된 비율은 0.5% 미만이라고 발표했습니다.

이는 회사가 제시한 수치이며, 전체 장비의 고장률과 동일하지는 않습니다.

5. 감가상각 내용연수

기존 1~3년에서 3~5년으로 변경한 이유는 연구개발용 장비에서 상업용 클라우드 장비까지 자산 구성이 확대됐기 때문이라고 설명했습니다.

TSMC 인증 원본, 실제 장기 운영 데이터, 전력 효율, OpenAI 계약의 경제성은 추가적인 독립 검증이 필요합니다.

나는 Cerebras 주식을 이미 전량 매도했습니다.

Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman just responded to Culper Research’s short report, directly challenging several of its biggest allegations.

Here are the key takeaways:

1. CHIP LIFESPAN: 2 YEARS VS. 33–100+ YEARS

Culper claimed Cerebras wafers last only 1.4–2.3 years.

Cerebras responded with some remarkable numbers:

• TSMC qualifies its wafers for 10 years of continuous operation at 105°C.
• Maximum operating temperature: 85°C.
• Actual fleet average: BELOW 65°C.
• Estimated lifespan at 85°C: 33 YEARS.
• Estimated lifespan at 65°C: OVER 100 YEARS.

These are theoretical estimates for heat-induced failure, not guaranteed lifespans. But they directly challenge the short seller’s central argument.

Even more importantly, Cerebras revealed that LESS THAN 0.5% of deployed CS-3 wafers have been decommissioned since the product launched in 2024.

2. CEREBRAS DENIES RELYING ON THIRD-PARTY TECHNOLOGY

Culper alleged Cerebras relied on a third-party connector called PariPoser to solve thermal expansion issues.

Cerebras categorically denies this, stating it has NEVER shipped a system containing PariPoser.

Instead, it uses its own patented engineering architecture developed years ago.

3. THE “DUMMY OPERATIONS” ALLEGATION

Culper claimed Cerebras runs unnecessary calculations to prevent chips from cooling and cracking.

Cerebras acknowledges using controlled operations to stabilize power and temperature, but says this is intentional engineering, not evidence of defective chips.

Feldman even points to NVIDIA’s B300 using a comparable technique.

4. DEPRECIATION AND MARGINS

Culper questioned Cerebras extending equipment depreciation from 1–3 years to 3–5 years, arguing it artificially inflated margins.

Cerebras explains the change reflects its transition from R&D equipment to production cloud infrastructure.

For comparison, major cloud providers often depreciate AI hardware over 5–6 years.

5. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR OPENAI AND PROFITABILITY

A major part of Culper’s bearish financial thesis assumes Cerebras hardware needs replacing approximately every 2 years.

If the hardware lasts substantially longer, that changes the economics of Cerebras’ cloud business, its replacement costs, and potentially the profitability of its OpenAI agreement.

The biggest takeaway isn’t that Cerebras chips will literally last 100 years. It’s that the company has presented technical calculations, manufacturer qualification standards, and real-world reliability data that directly challenge the short seller’s central assumption.

Cerebras is already transitioning toward its FOURTH generation of wafer-scale computing.

If the company continues delivering on its technology and reliability claims, I believe the market is dramatically underestimating the long-term opportunity here.

I’m long $CBRS and remain extremely bullish.

Figure 0: Flagship Monograph Vol. 09 — The Non-Fungible Die: Custom HBM4 Base Dies, The 3x P/E Fallacy, and the End of the Commodity Memory Short. Silicon & Infra AlphExecutive Abstract: The Anatomy of a Generational Mispricing
Over the past four weeks, global equity markets have succumbed to a recurring bout of cognitive dissonance. Macro cyclical allocators, traditional tech sell-side analysts, and cyclical hedge fund desks have driven the forward price-to-earnings multiples of leading memory producers—Micron Technology ($MU) and SK Hynix (000660.KS)—down into the 3.0x to 4.5x range
The intellectual justification for this valuation collapse is built entirely on historical trauma. Market participants look back at the brutal downcycles of 2018 and 2022, asserting with cynical certainty that "memory has been boom and bust since the 1970s, long-term agreements (LTAs) are meaningless paper, and customers will walk away the moment spot prices weaken.
This monograph demonstrates that this short thesis is built on an elementary category error: it applies legacy commodity DRAM economic models to an industry that has physically mutated into custom advanced logic foundry manufacturing
In Monograph #03: The 3:1 Wafer Squeeze, we established the solid-state manufacturing laws that govern HBM4: the irreversible cleanroom footprint of Through-Silicon Vias (TSV), the exponential yield degradation across 16-high stacks, and the thermo-mechanical warpage limits of Navier-Cauchy elasticity that forced the entire industry into TSMC's packaging ecosystem
This monograph serves as the direct sequel and ultimate commercial verdict. We prove that the structural break in memory is not merely a supply-side physical bottleneck, but a total destruction of spot market fungibility:
1. The Extinction of Spot Market Arbitrage: Unlike DDR3 or DDR4, which adhered to standardized JEDEC pinouts and could be sourced generically off spot exchanges in Shenzhen or Taipei, HBM4 features a 2,048-bit wide physical bus fabricated on TSMC's 3nm/4nm advanced logic nodes. Its microbump pinout, PHY routing, and Built-In Self-Test (BIST) circuitry are co-designed and taped out exclusively for specific accelerator architectures (such as Nvidia Vera Rubin or Google TPU). There is no spot market for custom logic dies.
2. The "Hostage Silicon" Contractual Lock: A hyperscaler attempting to breach an HBM4 take-or-pay agreement cannot simply substitute generic components. Walking away forfeits the entire custom logic tape-out, stranding tens of thousands of host GPUs and writing off billions in advanced packaging commitments. The default penalty is not a price adjustment; it is the death of the compute cluster itself.
3. The 816B Agentic Workload Mandate: Empirical telemetry from next-generation inference benchmarks (such as SemiAnalysis's preview of Vera Rubin running Muse Spark Open 816B) reveals that agentic reasoning loops and multi-turn context windows shift compute entirely into the memory-bandwidth-bound decode phase. Delivering 1,000 tokens/sec/user at P90 interactivity requires sustained bandwidth exceeding 20 TB/s per socket—a physical regime that only 2,048-bit custom HBM4 can service.
4. The Refutation of the 10% Revenue Myth: Bearish arguments claiming that HBM accounts for only 10% of memory revenue suffer from basic arithmetic errors that conflate total addressable market (TAM) with company-specific revenue. In a $100B 2027 HBM market, a 20% share generates $20B for Micron, representing ~40% of its consensus $50B top line and over 60% of total gross profit. Compounded by the 3.5:1 wafer crowd-out ratio, allocating 15% of bit production to HBM consumes over 40% of leading-edge wafer starts, locking commodity server DDR5 into an irreversible 20% to 22% structural supply deficit.
5. The Multiple Rerating: When non-cancellable custom silicon agreements eliminate downside cash flow volatility, treating memory producers as 3x P/E cyclicals represents the single largest valuation dislocation in modern semiconductor history. Applying an infrastructure cash flow discount rate (WACC compression from 11.5% to 7.5%) dictates a fundamental rerating toward 15x to 20x P/E, triggering a generational Davis Double Play.
Chapter I. The 3x P/E Fallacy: Commodity PTSD vs. Custom Foundry Reality
1.1 The Anatomy of the 2018 Trauma
To understand why Wall Street is currently mispricing memory stocks, one must examine the psychological scar tissue of the 2018–2019 collapse.
In late 2017, memory producers enjoyed peak operating margins exceeding 60%. Hyperscalers had engaged in panic buying of standard server DDR4 DIMMs. However, by mid-2018, as enterprise server demand cooled, cloud procurement desks abruptly halted purchasing.
Because DDR4 was a standardized commodity governed by JEDEC specifications, memory modules were 100% fungible:
• A 64GB DDR4-2666 ECC Registered DIMM produced by Samsung was electrically and physically interchangeable with an equivalent module produced by Micron or SK Hynix.
• When spot market prices dropped below contract prices, cloud buyers immediately breached verbal commitments, allowed existing inventories to burn down, and sourced distressed lots from the spot market at cash cost.
• Within four quarters, operating margins collapsed from +60% to single digits, and memory equities experienced peak-to-trough drawdowns of 40% to 55%.
Today's macro bears assume this exact sequence will replay in 2027. They point to forward multiples of 3.5x for Micron and 4.0x for SK Hynix as evidence that "smart money" is already pricing in the inevitable margin liquidation.
🔄 Commodity Memory vs. Bespoke AI Silicon Regime Comparison:
* Traditional Commodity DRAM Regime (DDR3 / DDR4 / Standard DDR5):
* Standard JEDEC Sockets → 100% Interchangeable Fungibility → High Spot Liquidity
* Downcycle Reality: Spot price crumbles → LTAs breached → Severe margin bust (2018)
* Modern AI Memory Regime (HBM3e / HBM4 / Custom Base Dies):
* Custom Silicon Tape-Out → Zero Spot Fungibility → Bilateral Monopoly Lock-in
* Downcycle Reality: Bespoke pinouts → Default scraps $50k+ GPU SiP → Cash flows intact (2027+)
1.2 The Fallacy of Applying Commodity Elasticity to Heterogeneous SiP
The flaw in this thesis lies in the assumption of product interchangeability.
A commodity market requires two prerequisites:
1. Standardized form factors allowing multiple suppliers to compete for an identical socket.
2. Low switching costs enabling buyers to arbitrage price differentials across vendors.
In HBM4, both prerequisites are physically non-existent. HBM4 is not an independent component sold on a circuit board; it is an integrated sub-element of a System-in-Package (SiP).
When an accelerator manufacturer like Nvidia or Google designs an ultra-high-performance package, the physical placement of the HBM cubes, the interposer routing lines, the microbump metallurgy, and the custom PHY layer inside the base die are finalized 24 months prior to mass production.
There is no secondary spot market for HBM4. You cannot buy an HBM4 stack from an open distributor, nor can an unallocated stack produced for an Nvidia Vera Rubin module be redirected to an AMD Helios chassis or a custom hyperscaler ASIC.
Pricing an asset class with zero secondary market liquidity and 100% bilateral co-design at a commodity cyclical multiple is an analytical failure.
Chapter II. The "Hostage Silicon" Mechanism: Co-Design, TSMC Base Dies & Contractual Lock-in
2.1 The Metamorphosis of the Logic Base Die
In earlier generations (HBM2e and HBM3), the base die at the bottom of the memory stack was manufactured by the memory vendors themselves using mature DRAM-adjacent processes (1y/1z nm). Its function was largely passive: simple test logic, power routing, and basic signal buffering.
With HBM4, the physical bus width doubles from 1,024 bits to 2,048 bits. This dramatic expansion in interconnect density requires over 40,000 microbumps per cube at an ultra-fine pitch of 25 µm to 30 µm. A standard DRAM process cannot achieve the routing density or the switching speeds required to drive 2,048 differential lines at multi-gigabit rates while maintaining low bit-error rates (BER).
Consequently, the industry has executed an irreversible structural shift: the HBM4 base die has migrated entirely to leading-edge foundry logic nodes—predominantly TSMC N3E and N4P.

I encourage those at frontier AI companies to read this quote, from Ellsberg to Kissinger back in 1968:

“Henry, there’s something I would like to tell you, for what it’s worth, something I wish I had been told years ago. You’ve been a consultant for a long time, and you’ve dealt a great deal with top secret information. But you’re about to receive a whole slew of special clearances, maybe fifteen or twenty of them, that are higher than top secret."

“I’ve had a number of these myself, and I’ve known other people who have just acquired them, and I have a pretty good sense of what the effects of receiving these clearances are on a person who didn’t previously know they even existed. And the effects of reading the information that they will make available to you."

“First, you’ll be exhilarated by some of this new information, and by having it all — so much! incredible! — suddenly available to you. But second, almost as fast, you will feel like a fool for having studied, written, talked about these subjects, criticized and analyzed decisions made by presidents for years without having known of the existence of all this information, which presidents and others had and you didn’t, and which must have influenced their decisions in ways you couldn’t even guess. In particular, you’ll feel foolish for having literally rubbed shoulders for over a decade with some officials and consultants who did have access to all this information you didn’t know about and didn’t know they had, and you’ll be stunned that they kept that secret from you so well."

“You will feel like a fool, and that will last for about two weeks. Then, after you’ve started reading all this daily intelligence input and become used to using what amounts to whole libraries of hidden information, which is much more closely held than mere top secret data, you will forget there ever was a time when you didn’t have it, and you’ll be aware only of the fact that you have it now and most others don’t….and that all those other people are fools."

“Over a longer period of time — not too long, but a matter of two or three years — you’ll eventually become aware of the limitations of this information. There is a great deal that it doesn’t tell you, it’s often inaccurate, and it can lead you astray just as much as the New York Times can. But that takes a while to learn."

“In the meantime it will have become very hard for you to learn from anybody who doesn’t have these clearances. Because you’ll be thinking as you listen to them: ‘What would this man be telling me if he knew what I know? Would he be giving me the same advice, or would it totally change his predictions and recommendations?’ And that mental exercise is so torturous that after a while you give it up and just stop listening. I’ve seen this with my superiors, my colleagues….and with myself."

“You will deal with a person who doesn’t have those clearances only from the point of view of what you want him to believe and what impression you want him to go away with, since you’ll have to lie carefully to him about what you know. In effect, you will have to manipulate him. You’ll give up trying to assess what he has to say. The danger is, you’ll become something like a moron. You’ll become incapable of learning from most people in the world, no matter how much experience they may have in their particular areas that may be much greater than yours.”

"….Kissinger hadn’t interrupted this long warning. As I’ve said, he could be a good listener, and he listened soberly. He seemed to understand that it was heartfelt, and he didn’t take it as patronizing, as I’d feared. But I knew it was too soon for him to appreciate fully what I was saying. He didn’t have the clearances yet."

People genuinely don't understand this:

1. The global average IQ is 84. It's not the only factor but it's a major one.

2. Most successful ethnic groups have an average IQ of 100-105. The highest (Ashkenazi Jews) sit at about 107-112.

3. In order for a society to thrive, it needs to have an average IQ over 100. 103-105 or so seems to be the threshold.

At 103-105, you get peak England, the Scandinavian countries or peak Germany. At 100 you get France, and at 98 Spain.

The difference between global domination and also-ran is surprisingly small; just 2-3 IQ points. Another 4-5 and you're a basket case country like the Philippines or Bulgaria or modern Greece.

4. IQ can, within a population, shift solely through genetics, by 0.5-1.0 points per generation.

Social factors can magnify that effect by 5-7 points.

Consequently, the functional IQ of a population can change enough in one generation for a society to go from "world domination" to " basket case."

A more realistic outcome is that this can take 2 or 3 generations to happen. Well, that is what happened.

People often misinterpret the Flynn effect and think that IQs are rising but they're not. They're declining.

5. America is now too low IQ to maintain its position as world hegemon. More so, current birthrate trends have us rapidly entering not just "also ran" territory but "basket case."

The only reason we will stay on top is because we're absurdly rich compared to the rest of the world so we have a long way to fall before anyone catches us.

6. Successful countries become successful usually through a long process of breeding themselves into a higher IQ and then matching that with a social organization that maximizes it.

All it takes is one bad generation to destroy what took centuries to gain.

This is why today's Greeks aren't like the Greeks of golden age antiquity, and today's Romans aren't like the Romans of old. 

7. The highest IQ populations today are both not reproducing but also replacing themselves with low IQ populations.

Even Israel is only 1/3 Ashkenazi with lower IQ groups making up the majority of the country. It is worth noting that the Haredi (the cohort with the highest total fertility rate) is about 80% Ashkenazi, but I have no available data on their average IQ.

My point is that IQ does not appear to be an evolutionary advantage in the modern age and as such, it isn't being selected for.

This suggests that we're in a race against decline. We need to solve the IQ problem through technology before we simply run out of smart people living in functioning societies.
